§ ScopeGuard

Turn a client’s “small favor” into an evidence-backed, estimated change order.

For freelance web developers and small agencies. The machine reads, quotes, and keeps every version straight — the human decides, prices, and sends.

Live demo follows this deck · working sample project at /demo

The problem

“One more small thing before we launch.”

Inbox — Dana, Northwind Bakerythis morning

Hi, thanks for sending the mockups over — they look great overall. A few things we’d like to sort out before launch:

Could you add online ordering so customers can pay for pickup orders through the site? We’d also like customer accounts so regulars can save their favourite items.

Quite a few of our customers speak Portuguese, so we’d like the site available in Portuguese as well as English… and can we add a separate page for each of our three locations?

Let me know what’s involved. Thanks, Dana

Never actually small: Four of Dana’s five asks fall outside agreed scope. Answering well means finding the exact contract clause.

The idea

The machine reads.
The human decides.

Existing tools split into two camps: trackers that know work exists but nothing about the contract, and AI review that makes financial judgments. ScopeGuard refuses both halves of that trade.

What the machine does

  • Reads the whole agreement

    every clause, every time — nothing half-remembered

  • Quotes it verbatim

    exact sentence, highlighted where it lives in the SOW

  • Keeps versions straight

    append-only AI output, separate from your decisions

What only the human does

  • Decides

    confirm or override every label — your recorded decision

  • Prices

    hours stay NULL until a human types them

  • Sends

    ScopeGuard never transmits directly to your client

How it works

Four steps, two human moments

  1. 1

    Paste the scope and the request

    Upload a PDF (text-layer, or scanned with OCR behind mandatory human review) or paste text.

  2. 2

    See what the contract says

    Each ask is labelled with verified source quote attached verbatim character-by-character.

  3. 3

    You decide and you price

    Confirm or override every label; enter hours. Your review is stored separately from AI output.

  4. 4

    Get the change order

    Deterministic template, one totals formula everywhere — screen, client reply, PDF, frozen snapshot.

The trust spine

Three guarantees, enforced in code — not requested of the model

Statement of Work — §3 Languagesverified

The site will be provided in English only. Translation into additional languages is not included and would be quoted separately.

Dana asks for Portuguese. ScopeGuard quotes verbatim & offset-mapped. A quote not in the document is rejected. ✓ verified citation
  • 1

    Absence from document is never treated as exclusion

    potentially_additional + no verified evidence → needs_clarification

    A hallucinated citation degrades safely into an honest question instead of hardening into a billable claim. Also neutralizes prompt injection.

  • 2

    The model never supplies a number

    The schema has no field for hours, cost, or dates — there is nowhere to put one. Generated prose is scanned and scrubbed.

  • 3

    AI output, decisions, and final documents are separate records

    Re-running an analysis writes new assessments without touching reviews. Finalized documents are frozen by triggers.

The refusal is the feature

A final change order cannot carry a blank

ScopeGuard will not finalize a change order containing additional work with no human-entered hours. The button is disabled in the database until every line is priced by a person.

“A draft can carry open questions. A final change order cannot.”

  • §

    Hours stay NULL

    until a human types them — the schema has nowhere else to put one.

  • §

    One totals formula

    BigInt on integer minor units, half-up rounding — screen, reply, PDF, and invoice match by construction.

  • §

    Finalizing freezes a snapshot

    Editing a draft can never change what a previously sent document said.

Architecture

Model output never reaches the user directly

  • 1

    Trust spine is the single gatekeeper

    Model output passes through citation verifier and safe-downgrade before any UI render.

  • 2

    External services strictly isolated

    OpenAI API with strict json_schema; Slack OAuth tokens encrypted with AES-256-GCM.

  • 3

    Supabase Postgres with RLS on every table

    Zero service-role keys anywhere. The public demo acts through Supabase anonymous auth with full RLS.

Every code path acts as a signed-in user and goes through row-level security. Nothing in the app can bypass it.

Integrations & boundaries

Notifications announce. They never act.

Gmail drafts (never send), CRM sync (outbound-only), and payment links scaffolded honestly.

Slack — per-user OAuth, wired for real

  • Each user connects their own workspace

    Standard SaaS OAuth pattern — operator registers one app, users authorize their own.

  • Tokens encrypted at rest

    AES-256-GCM; owner-only by RLS — database dumps yield no usable tokens.

  • Finalizing posts to your channel

    Through user’s own connection; failed notification never fails finalization.

Two things it will never do

  • Contact your client

    “Open in Gmail” opens your compose window pre-filled — you press send.

  • Change a figure or status

    Notifications only report finalized snapshots — they cannot alter them.
